problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 10 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,-1),(0,2),$ and $(-2,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(6,-1)$
- $(7,-14)$
- $(8,-16)$
worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 10 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -6 & 7 \\ -16 & 12 & -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(8,-16),$ $(-6,12)$, and $(7,-14).$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."
